    INITIAL BRIEF OF INTERVENOR AARON C. BECHTER (TRACT 3509)
         Post-Hearing Initial Brief Following the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

Intervenor Aaron C. Bechter ("Mr. Bechter" or "Intervenor"), appearing prose as the intervenor of
record for Tract 3509, respectfully submits this Initial Brief following the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing
on the Merits in the above-styled and -numbered proceeding, and would respectfully show the
Administrative Law Judges ("ALJs") the following.


I. STATEMENT OF THE CASE AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY
This proceeding concerns the joint application of On cor Electric Delivery Company LLC ("On cor")
and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation ("LCRA TSC," and together with Oncor,
"Applicants") to amend their respective Certificates of Convenience and Necessity ("CCN") to
construct, own, and operate the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV
Transmission Line Project (the "Project"). Among the alternative routes presented for the
Commission's consideration are Segment A2, an alignment that would cross or closely approach
Intervenor's property, and Segment A3, an alternative alignment that would avoid Intervenor's
property and the immediately surrounding rural community. Notably, Applicants' own Initial Post-
Hearing Brief, filed in this docket on June 19, 2026, does not advocate for the selection of
Segment A2 or any other specific route; it states that "Applicants do not object to the selection of
any filed route or constructible combination of forward-progressing alternative route links," and
that Applicants will construct whatever route the Commission selects among the 122 routes
presented in the Application.

Mr. Bechter is the owner of Tract 3509, the residential property located at 8564 Shaw Road,
Rogers, Texas 76569, in Bell County. Mr. Bechter intervened in this proceeding in his individual
capacity as the owner of Tract 3509. His wife, Alison Bechter, is a separate, independently-
represented prose intervenor of record with respect to Tract 3510, the adjoining ten-acre parcel.
Mr. Bechter and Ms. Bechter have filed separate testimony, separate exhibits, and separate
briefing in this docket, and each relies on his or her own personal knowledge of his or her own
tract. This Brief addresses only Mr. Bechter's position as to Tract 3509.




PUC Docket No. 59475/ SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter   Page 1 of 8
 Mr. Bechter filed his Direct Testimony and Statement of Position in this docket on May 12, 2026,
in advance of the Commission's prefiled testimony deadline. Applicants thereafter filed objections
to, and a motion to strike, portions of the prefiled testimony of multiple intervenors. On June 3,
2026, Mr. Bechter filed his Prehearing Exhibit List (Exhibits A through N) and Witness List,
identifying himself as his own sole witness. Following the June 5, 2026 prehearing conference,
the ALJs convened a Hearing on the Merits, which proceeded from June 8 through June 12, 2026.

During the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits, the ALJs denied Applicants' Motion to Strike
in its entirety. Mr. Bechter's Direct Testimony and Statement of Position was admitted into the
evidentiary record as filed, without change, limitation, or redaction. His exhibits - including
Exhibits G, H, and M, which are letters from Texas state legislators placing the Commission on
notice of landowner and community concerns regarding the Project, offered for the limited, non-
hearsay purpose of establishing notice to the Commission rather than the truth of the matters
asserted therein -were likewise admitted. Applicants' counsel did not press a hearsay or other
objection to those exhibits at hearing. Mr. Bechter was not called for cross-examination by any
party. His Direct Testimony and exhibits therefore stand in the record unrebutted.

Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6 and SOAH Order No. 32 (Addressing Post-Hearing Matters, Jun.
15, 2026), Initial Briefs are due no later than 11:59 p.m. Central Time on June 19, 2026, with
Reply Briefs and Proposed Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Ordering Paragraphs due
June 26, 2026. Mr. Bechter timely files this Initial Brief in accordance with that schedule.


II. SUMMARY OF ARGUMENT
Applicants bear the burden of proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, that Segment A2 is
necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public under PURA §
37.056(a), and that the routing of Segment A2 properly accounts for the factors enumerated in
PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (b)(3)(B), including community values,
environmental integrity, and the Commission's policy of prudent avoidance.

The unrebutted record contains sworn testimony establishing concrete, present, and ongoing
harm to Mr. Bechter from Segment A2 as proposed. Mr. Bechter's residence - the habitable
structure most directly implicated by the prudent-avoidance analysis applicable to this proceeding
- sits approximately 1,583.92 feet from the proposed Segment A2 structures. Tract 3509
maintains an active agricultural property tax exemption that depends on uninterrupted qualifying
use, and the surrounding road infrastructure on which Mr. Bechter and his family rely already
shows measurable degradation from existing energy-development traffic, a condition Segment
A2 construction would compound.

Applicants offered no evidence at hearing controverting Mr. Bechter's testimony, and no evidence
explaining why Segment A2, rather than Segment A3 or another alignment that avoids Tract 3509,
best satisfies the statutory and regulatory routing criteria. The disproportion in landowner
opposition is itself probative: by Intervenor's review of the Commission's docket activity in this
proceeding, approximately twenty-four landowners have intervened in opposition to alignments
along Segment A2, compared to a single intervenor or protestant associated with Segment A3.



PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter   Page 2 of 8
 That disparity bears directly on the "community values" and impact-moderation factors the
Commission must weigh under PURA § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code§ 25.101 (b)(3)(B).

Because Applicants have not carried their burden as to Segment A2, and because the unrebutted
record establishes that a materially less-impactful alternative remains available, the Commission
should decline to approve Segment A2 to the extent it affects Tract 3509, and should give full and
serious weight to Segment A3 or any alignment that avoids Mr. Bechter's property.


Ill. BURDEN OF PROOF AND STANDARD OF REVIEW
Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA"), the Commission "may approve an application
and grant a certificate only if the commission finds that the certificate is necessary for the service,
accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public." PURA § 37.056(a) (Tex. Util. Code Ann. §
37.056(a)). In making that determination, and in particular in selecting among alternative routes,
the Commission must consider the factors set out in PURA § 37.056(c), including the adequacy
of existing service, the need for additional service, and "other factors, such as (A) community
values; (B) recreational and park areas; (C) historical and aesthetic values; [and] (D)
environmental integrity." PURA § 37.056(c)(4). The Commission's own substantive rule
implementing these statutory routing factors, 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (b)(3)(B), further
requires consideration of whether a proposed route uses or parallels existing compatible rights-
of-way, whether it parallels property lines or natural or cultural features, and whether it conforms
with the Commission's policy of "prudent avoidance" - defined under 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101 (a)(6) as "the limiting of exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with
reasonable investments of money and effort." These factors "are stated in the broadest possible
terms and are intended as legislative standards to guide the Commission in its administration of
the certification process," to be considered only in the context of the case at hand and weighed
against one another where they compete. Hammack v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 131 S.W.3d
713, 719, 723, 727 (Tex. App.-Austin 2004); Pub. Util. Comm'n v. Texland Elec. Co., 701 S.W.2d
261, 266 (Tex. App.-Austin 1985); see also Dunn v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 246 S.W.3d 788,
794 (Tex. App.-Austin 2008).

As the parties seeking affirmative relief and seeking to change the status quo by obtaining
authority to construct new 765-kV transmission infrastructure across private property that does
not presently host such infrastructure, Applicants bear the burden of proof in this proceeding. See
1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.427 (identifying the party seeking affirmative relief and the party
seeking to change the status quo as the party ordinarily bearing the burden of proof in SOAH
contested-case proceedings). That burden must be carried by a preponderance of the evidence.
See Granek v. Tex. State Bd. of Med. Exam'rs, 172 S.W.3d 761, 777 (Tex. App.-Austin 2005,
no pet.). Where, as here, Applicants offered no evidence at hearing rebutting an intervenor's
sworn, unchallenged testimony of specific and concrete harm, and offered no comparative routing
evidence addressing that harm, the preponderance standard is not met as to the route segment
affecting that intervenor's property.


IV. STATEMENT OF FACTS- EVIDENCE OF RECORD


PUC Docket No. 59475/ SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349- Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter    Page 3 of 8
 A. Intervenor's Standing and Property
Mr. Bechter owns and resides at Tract 3509, the residential property at 8564 Shaw Road, Rogers,
Texas, with his wife. His standing in this proceeding rests on his ownership of Tract 3509 and on
his personal, firsthand knowledge of the use, character, and conditions of that property, as set
forth in his Direct Testimony and Statement of Position, admitted into evidence during the June
8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits without limitation.

B. Proximity of Proposed Segment A2 to the Residence
As established in Mr. Bechter's admitted Direct Testimony and supporting exhibits, the structures
proposed for Segment A2 would be located approximately 1,583.92 feet from his residence- a
habitable structure occupied year-round by Mr. Bechter and his family. This measurement is
based on Mr. Bechter's personal review of Applicants' own routing materials and publicly available
mapping data, and is unrebutted in the record. Because the residence is a habitable structure, its
proximity to the proposed Segment A2 centerline places it squarely within the category of impacts
the Commission's prudent-avoidance policy under 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (a)(6) is
designed to address.

C. Agricultural Use and the Active Exemption
Tract 3509 maintains an active agricultural property tax exemption based on hay production, and
Mr. Bechter also raises chickens on the property. Mr. Bechter has concrete, specific plans to
expand into cattle grazing and beekeeping. Maintaining the existing exemption, like qualifying for
one in the first instance, depends on the continuity of qualifying agricultural use; construction
activity, easement clearing, and access-road work associated with Segment A2 threaten to disrupt
that continuity in the same manner addressed in the related Initial Brief filed by Intervenor Alison
Bechter as to the adjoining Tract 3510.

D. Road Degradation and Compounding Infrastructure Impact
Mr. Bechter has personally observed significant degradation of Shaw Road resulting from heavy
construction traffic associated with nearby solar development. He raised these concerns directly
with Bell County Precinct 2 Commissioner Greg Reynolds, who personally visited the property to
assess road conditions, and Mr. Bechter separately documented his concerns through a call to
the Bell County Road and Bridge Department. The addition of construction traffic associated with
Segment A2 - heavy equipment, crane traffic, and material delivery - would compound an
already-documented condition on the same rural road network on which Mr. Bechter's family
depends for daily access, emergency services, and school transportation.

E. Rural Character, Environmental, and Cumulative Impact
Mr. Bechter has personally observed the cumulative industrialization of the rural corridor
surrounding Tract 3509, including nearby solar development, displacement of wildlife, and
increased coyote activity in the immediate vicinity of his property. These firsthand observations
are relevant to the "environmental integrity" and "community values" factors the Commission must
weigh under PURA § 37.056(c)(4), and they establish that Segment A2 would not be imposed on



PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter   Page 4 of 8
 an undisturbed rural landscape, but on a community already absorbing substantial cumulative
energy-infrastructure impact.

F. Notice to the Commission -        Admitted Legislative Correspondence
Exhibits G, H, and M, admitted during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing on the Merits, consist of
letters submitted to the Commission by Texas state legislators - dated April 29, 2026, May 5,
2026, and May 11, 2026, respectively - documenting legislative concern regarding the Project
and the broader pace of the Commission's review of proposed 765-kV transmission infrastructure
across the affected region. These exhibits were, and remain, offered solely for the limited, non-
hearsay purpose of establishing that the Commission has been placed on formal notice of these
concerns, not for the truth of the matters asserted in them. Their admission without sustained
objection confirms that this is properly part of the evidentiary record before the Commission in
evaluating the public-interest and community-values factors applicable to this proceeding.


V.ARGUMENT

A. Applicants Have Not Carried Their Burden Under PURA § 37.056 as to Segment A2
PURA § 37.056(a) permits the Commission to grant the requested CCN amendment only upon a
finding that it is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public.
That finding, where the application presents multiple route alternatives, necessarily requires the
Commission to evaluate whether the specific route selected - here, Segment A2 - reflects
appropriate consideration of the factors in PURA § 37.056(c), including community values and
environmental integrity. Applicants presented no evidence during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing
on the Merits rebutting Mr. Bechter's unchallenged testimony regarding the proximity of Segment
A2 to his residence, the risk to his property's agricultural exemption, or the compounding road-
infrastructure harm Segment A2 would impose, and no evidence explaining why that harm is
outweighed by any corresponding benefit specific to the A2 alignment as opposed to Segment
A3 or another route that avoids Tract 3509. Indeed, Applicants' own Initial Post-Hearing Brief
confirms that they press no such case: Applicants ask the ALJs to recommend approval "along
any filed route" and state that they "do not object to the selection of any filed route or constructible
 combination of forward-progressing alternative route links." Applicants having declined to defend
 Segment A2 specifically, there is no evidentiary or argumentative basis in this record on which
the Commission could find that Segment A2, rather than Segment A3 or another alignment
 avoiding Tract 3509, satisfies PURA § 37.056(c). On this record, Applicants have not carried their
 burden by a preponderance of the evidence as to Segment A2 insofar as it affects Tract 3509.

B. The Routing Criteria of 16 Tex. Admin. Code§ 25.101(b)(3J(B) Do Not Favor Segment
A2 Over an Alignment That Avoids the Residence at Tract 3509
Section 25.101 (b)(3)(B) directs the Commission to consider, among other things, whether a route
conforms with the policy of prudent avoidance. Prudent avoidance does not require routing
decisions to eliminate all proximity between transmission infrastructure and habitable structures;
it requires the Commission to favor reasonable, available alternatives that limit exposure and
impact "with reasonable investments of money and effort." 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101 (a)(6).


PUC Docket No. 59475/ SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter     Page 5 of 8
 The Commission has previously found that prudent avoidance is achieved by minimizing the
number of habitable structures located in close proximity to a proposed route, see Joint
Application of Elec. Transmission Tex., LLC & Sharyland Utils. to Amend Their CCNs for the North
Edinburg to Lama Alta Double-Circuit 345-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 41606, FOF No. 64
(Apr. 11, 2011 ), and that routing along property boundaries or fencelines while avoiding habitable
structures helps preserve the community values and recreational-area factors that PURA §
37.056(c) requires the Commission to weigh. See Application of Brazos Elec. Power Coop., Inc.
to Amend a CCN for a Proposed Transmission Line Within Cooke Cnty., Docket No. 20516, FOF
No. 85 (Jan. 26, 2001). These precedents are particularly apt here, where the structure at issue
is not vacant land but Mr. Bechter's year-round residence. Here, a reasonable, already-identified
alternative - Segment A3 - exists and is before the Commission in this same proceeding.
Applicants have not shown, by evidence presented at hearing, why selecting that reasonable
alternative, or another alignment that avoids the residence at Tract 3509, would not satisfy the
public need that Applicants assert while materially reducing the impact on Mr. Bechter, his family,
and the surrounding community.

C. The Disparity in Landowner Opposition Confirms Segment A2 Fails to Moderate
Impact on the Affected Community
The "community values" factor under PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A) is not an abstraction; the
Commission has defined it as "a shared appreciation of an area or other mutual resource by a
national, regional, or local community," with adverse effects consisting of "those aspects of a
proposed project that would significantly alter the use, enjoyment, or intrinsic value attached to
an important area or resource by a community." Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Round Rock-Leander 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 45866,
Order on Rehearing, FOF No. 37 (Jul. 28, 2017); Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Proposed EC Mornhinweg to Parkway 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket
No. 40684, FOF 43 (Jun. 19, 2013). That impact is measured, in part, by the lived response of
the community to the route as proposed. By Intervenor's review of the Commission's docket
activity in this proceeding, approximately twenty-four landowners have intervened in opposition
to alignments along Segment A2, while only a single intervenor or protestant is associated with
Segment A3. Intervenor recognizes that, pursuant to SOAH Order No. 24 (Ruling on Intervenor
Motions, Granting Leave for Late-Filed Testimonies, and Dismissing Intervenors, Jun. 1, 2026),
a substantial number of intervenors in this large, fifteen-county proceeding were dismissed for
procedural reasons unrelated to the merits of their concerns; that history does not diminish the
 relevance of the disparity among the intervenors who remained eligible to participate at hearing,
 but Intervenor respectfully requests that the Commission independently confirm the precise
figures from its own docket records. The Commission should take into account the magnitude of
this disparity, as it bears directly and substantially on whether Segment A2, as proposed, reflects
 the degree of community-impact moderation that PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code§
 25.101 (b)(3)(B) require. This conclusion is consistent with the position of the Office of Public Utility
 Counsel, which in its own Post-Hearing Initial Brief filed in this docket on June 18, 2026, urged
 the Commission to scrutinize this application "with the aim of having the fewest number of
 landowners ... affected by approval of this project," and to give the concerns raised by pro se
 intervenors equal footing with those raised by represented parties.



 PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter     Page 6 of 8
 D. Compounding Harm to Shared Rural Infrastructure Warrants Particular Weight
The road degradation Mr. Bechter has personally documented, and which Bell County's own
Precinct 2 Commissioner found sufficiently concerning to warrant a personal site visit, is not a
hypothetical future impact - it is an existing, observable condition. Adding Segment A2
construction traffic to that already-strained rural road network, rather than routing the Project
along Segment A3 or another alignment with less impact on the immediate Shaw Road corridor,
would compound a documented harm without any showing in this record that doing so is
necessary to meet Applicants' stated public-interest objectives.

E. The Record Evidence of Mounting Legislative Concern Supports a Cautious, Fully-
Informed Routing Decision
Exhibits G, H, and M- properly admitted at hearing for the limited purpose of establishing notice
to the Commission -demonstrate that elected representatives of the affected region have, over
a period of weeks, repeatedly and formally communicated concern to the Commission regarding
the pace and scope of review applicable to this and related 765-kV transmission proposals. While
these exhibits are not offered for the truth of the specific factual assertions they contain, their
admission confirms that the Commission has been placed on notice, through its own docket, that
the routing decision in this proceeding is one of substantial and growing public and legislative
concern - reinforcing the importance of a full and careful application of the statutory and
regulatory routing criteria before approving Segment A2.


VI. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER FOR RELIEF
For the foregoing reasons, Intervenor Aaron C. Bechter respectfully requests that the
Administrative Law Judges find and recommend, and that the Commission ultimately determine,
that Applicants have not met their burden under PURA § 37.056 to show that Segment A2 is
necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public insofar as that
segment affects Tract 3509. Mr. Bechter further requests that the Commission decline to approve
Segment A2 as it affects Tract 3509, and instead give full and serious weight to Segment A3, or
to any alternative alignment that avoids Tract 3509, consistent with the Commission's policy of
prudent avoidance and the routing criteria of PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101 (b)(3)(8). Mr. Bechter's ultimate position is, and has consistently been, opposition to the
physical proximity of 765-kV transmission infrastructure to Tract 3509 - not opposition to any
particular segment label - and he requests that any route the Commission ultimately approves
avoid his property.

In the alternative, should the Commission nonetheless approve Segment A2 in a manner that
affects Tract 3509, Mr. Bechter respectfully requests that the Commission order implementation
of optimum phasing and any other reasonable, available mitigation measures the Commission
has required in prior dockets to minimize electric and magnetic field exposure and other impacts
to the residence, consistent with the Commission's policy of prudent avoidance. See, e.g.,
Application of Cross Tex. Transmission, LLC to Amend its CCN for the Limestone to Gibbons
Creek 345-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 44649, FOF No. 237 (Jan. 13, 2016). Mr. Bechter
further requests that the Commission order such road-protection, repair, or maintenance


PUC Docket No. 59475 I SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 -Initial Brief of Aaron C. Bechter   Page 7 of 8
 commitments as are reasonable and available to address the cumulative road-infrastructure
impact described above. Mr. Bechter further requests such other and further relief, at law or in
equity, to which he may show himself justly entitled.

serious weight to Segment A3 or any alignment that avoids Mr. Bechter's property.


Ill. BURDEN OF PROOF AND STANDARD OF REVIEW
Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA"), the Commission "may approve an application
and grant a certificate only if the commission finds that the certificate is necessary for the service,
accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public." PURA § 37.056(a) (Tex. Util. Code Ann. §
37.056(a)). In making that determination, and in particular in selecting among alternative routes,
the Commission must consider the factors set out in PURA § 37.056(c), including the adequacy
of existing service, the need for additional service, and "other factors, such as (A) community
values; (B) recreational and park areas; (C) historical and aesthetic values; [and] (D)
environmental integrity." PURA § 37.056(c)(4). The Commission's own substantive rule
implementing these statutory routing factors, 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B), further
requires consideration of whether a proposed route uses or parallels existing compatible rights-
of-way, whether it parallels property lines or natural or cultural features, and whether it conforms
with the Commission's policy of "prudent avoidance" - defined under 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101(a)(6) as "the limiting of exposures to electric and magnetic fields that can be avoided with
reasonable investments of money and effort." These factors "are stated in the broadest possible
terms and are intended as legislative standards to guide the Commission in its administration of
the certification process," to be considered only in the context of the case at hand and weighed
against one another where they compete. Hammack v. Pub. Uti[. Comm'n of Tex., 131 S.W.3d
713,719,723,727 (Tex. App.-Austin 2004); Pub. Util. Comm'n v. Texland Elec. Co.,701 S.W.2d
261, 266 (Tex. App.-Austin 1985); see also Dunn v. Pub. Util. Comm'n of Tex., 246 S.W.3d 788,
794 (Tex. App.-Austin 2008)

As the parties seeking affirmative relief and seeking to change the status quo by obtaining
authority to construct new 765-kV transmission infrastructure across private property that does
not presently host such infrastructure, Applicants bear the burden of proof in this proceeding. See
1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.427 (identifying the party seeking affirmative relief and the party
seeking to change the status quo as the party ordinarily bearing the burden of proof in SOAH
contested-case proceedings). That burden must be carried by a preponderance of the evidence.
See Granek v. Tex. State Bd. of Med. Exam'rs, 172 S.W.3d 761, 777 (Tex. App.-Austin 2005,
no pet.). Where, as here, Applicants offered no evidence at hearing rebutting an intervenor's
sworn, unchallenged testimony of specific and concrete harm, and offered no comparative routing
evidence addressing that harm, the preponderance standard is not met as to the route segment
affecting that intervenor's property.

V. ARGUMENT
A. Applicants Have Not Carried Their Burden Under PURA § 37.056 as to Segment A2
PURA § 37.056(a) permits the Commission to grant the requested CCN amendment only upon a
finding that it is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the public.
That finding, where the application presents multiple route alternatives, necessarily requires the
Commission to evaluate whether the specific route selected - here, Segment A2 - reflects
appropriate consideration of the factors in PURA § 37.056(c), including community values and
environmental integrity. Applicants presented no evidence during the June 8-12, 2026 Hearing
on the Merits rebutting Mr. Bechter's unchallenged testimony regarding the proximity of Segment
A2 to his residence, the risk to his property's agricultural exemption, or the compounding road-
infrastructure harm Segment A2 would impose, and no evidence explaining why that harm is
outweighed by any corresponding benefit specific to the A2 alignment as opposed to Segment
A3 or another route that avoids Tract 3509. Indeed, Applicants' own Initial Post-Hearing Brief
confirms that they press no such case: Applicants ask the ALJs to recommend approval "along
any filed route" and state that they "do not object to the selection of any filed route or constructible
combination of forward-progressing alternative route links." Applicants having declined to defend
Segment A2 specifically, there is no evidentiary or argumentative basis in this record on which
the Commission could find that Segment A2, rather than Segment A3 or another alignment
avoiding Tract 3509, satisfies PURA § 37.056(c). On this record, Applicants have not carried their
burden by a preponderance of the evidence as to Segment A2 insofar as it affects Tract 3509.

B. The Routing Criteria of 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B) Do Not Favor Segment
A2 Over an Alignment That Avoids the Residence at Tract 3509
Section 25.101(b)(3)(B) directs the Commission to consider, among other things, whether a route
conforms with the policy of prudent avoidance. Prudent avoidance does not require routing
decisions to eliminate all proximity between transmission infrastructure and habitable structures;
it requires the Commission to favor reasonable, available alternatives that limit exposure and
impact "with reasonable investments of money and effort." 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(a)(6)

 The Commission has previously found that prudent avoidance is achieved by minimizing the
number of habitable structures located in close proximity to a proposed route, see Joint
Application of Elec. Transmission Tex., LLC & Sharyland Utils. to Amend Their CCNs forthe North
Edinburg to Loma Alta Double-Circuit 345-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 41606, FOF No. 64
(Apr. 11, 2011), and that routing along property boundaries or fencelines while avoiding habitable
structures helps preserve the community values and recreational-area factors that PURA §
37.056(c) requires the Commission to weigh. See Application of Brazos Elec. Power Coop., Inc.
to Amend a CCN for a Proposed Transmission Line Within Cooke Cnty., Docket No. 20516, FOF
No. 85 (Jan. 26, 2001). These precedents are particularly apt here, where the structure at issue
is not vacant land but Mr. Bechter's year-round residence. Here, a reasonable, already-identified
alternative - Segment A3 - exists and is before the Commission in this same proceeding.
Applicants have not shown, by evidence presented at hearing, why selecting that reasonable
alternative, or another alignment that avoids the residence at Tract 3509, would not satisfy the
public need that Applicants assert while materially reducing the impact on Mr. Bechter, his family,
and the surrounding community.

C. The Disparity in Landowner Opposition Confirms Segment A2 Fails to Moderate
impact on the Affected Community
The "community values" factor under PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A) is not an abstraction; the
Commission has defined it as "a shared appreciation of an area or other mutual resource by a
national, regional, or local communityi with adverse effects consisting of "those aspects of a
proposed project that would significantly alter the use, enjoyment, or intrinsic value attached to
an important area or resource by a community." Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Round Rock-Leander 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket No. 45866,
Order on Rehearing, FOF No. 37 (Jul. 28, 2017); Application of LCRA Transmission Servs. Corp.
to Amend a CCN for the Proposed EC Mornhinweg to Parkway 138-kV Transmission Line, Docket
No. 40684, FOF 43 (Jun. 19, 2013). That impact is measured, in part, by the lived response of
the community to the route as proposed. By Intervenor's review of the Commission's docket
activity in this proceeding, approximately twenty-four landowners have intervened in opposition
to alignments along Segment A2, while only a single intervenor or protestant is associated with
Segment A3. Intervenor recognizes that, pursuant to SOAH Order No. 24 (Ruling on Intervenor
Motions, Granting Leave for Late-Filed Testimonies, and Dismissing Intervenors, Jun. 1,2026),
a substantial number of intervenors in this large, fifteen-county proceeding were dismissed for
procedural reasons unrelated to the merits of their concerns; that history does not diminish the
relevance of the disparity among the intervenors who remained eligible to participate at hearing,
but Intervenor respectfully requests that the Commission independently confirm the precise
figures from its own docket records. The Commission should take into account the magnitude of
this disparity, as it bears directly and substantially on whether Segment A2, as proposed, reflects
the degree of community-impact moderation that PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 Tex. Admin. Code §
25.101(b)(3)(B) require. This conclusion is consistent with the position of the Office of Public Utility
Counsel, which in its own Post-Hearing Initial Brief filed in this docket on June 18, 2026, urged
the Commission to scrutinize this application "with the aim of having the fewest number of
 landowners... affected by approval of this project," and to give the concerns raised by pro se
 intervenors equal footing with those raised by represented parties.
